title: Disaster Management & Sustainable Development
intro: Concise Notes for Competitive Exams — Extended Edition (lectures + online material, diagrams, MCQs & links)
Master handbook covering: Disaster Management + Sustainable Development + Exam Practice Pack
Overlapping topics have been merged into one chapter and repeated points removed. Practice MCQs for all parts are near the end; the answer key is the last chapter.

b: Hazard: process/phenomenon that may cause loss of life, injury, property damage, social or environmental disruption.
Natural: geophysical (earthquake, tsunami, volcano, landslide), hydro-meteorological (flood, cyclone, drought, heatwave), biological (epidemic).
Man-made / technological: industrial accidents, fire, explosions, chemical leaks, dam failure, nuclear.
Socio-natural: hazards made worse by human activity (e.g. floods due to deforestation, urban flooding).
Disaster: serious disruption of a community's functioning that exceeds its capacity to cope using its own resources.
Vulnerability: susceptibility to harm (physical, social, economic, environmental).
Exposure: people, property and systems located in hazard zones.
Capacity: strengths and resources available to manage risk. Coping capacity: ability to manage adverse conditions with available resources.
Resilience: ability to resist, absorb, accommodate, adapt to and recover from a hazard in a timely manner.
Risk formula: Risk = Hazard × Vulnerability (expanded: R = H × E × V / C).
Rapid-onset: earthquake, flash flood, tsunami. Slow-onset: drought, desertification, sea-level rise.
Secondary / cascading hazards: e.g. earthquake → landslide, tsunami, fire, liquefaction.
Build Back Better (BBB): use recovery to reduce future risk.

chapters.t: Hazard Profile & Major Disasters of Pakistan
b: Most frequent & damaging hazard: floods (monsoon season July–Sept).
Others: earthquakes, droughts (Thar, Cholistan, Balochistan), cyclones (Arabian Sea), landslides, GLOFs, heatwaves, smog, avalanches, tsunami (Makran Subduction Zone).
Glaciers: 7,000+ in northern Pakistan; ~3,000 glacial lakes, ~33 identified as GLOF-prone (UNDP GLOF project).
Mw 7.6; near Muzaffarabad; ~73,000+ deaths in Pakistan; led to NDMA, ERRA, BCP-SP 2007
Mw 7.7; new mud island off Gwadar coast
~33 million affected; ~1,739 deaths; ~1/3 of country under water; Sindh & Balochistan worst; PDNA: damage ≈ $14.9 bn, losses ≈ $15.2 bn, needs ≈ $16.3 bn
Extended material (beyond the lectures — standard textbooks & online sources)
2025 monsoon floods: NDMA reported about 1,006 deaths nationwide in the 2025 monsoon season, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa worst hit (flash floods e.g., Buner) followed by Punjab.
2022 floods: Record monsoon rains submerged about one-third of the country (mainly Sindh & Balochistan); ≈ 1,700 deaths and damages/losses of ≈ US$ 30 billion (PDNA estimate).
💡 Exam point: Pakistan is consistently ranked among the countries most affected by climate-related disasters (floods, heatwaves, GLOFs, droughts).
Focus/hypocenter: point of origin underground. Epicenter: point on surface directly above.
Body waves: P-wave (primary, longitudinal, fastest, through solids & liquids); S-wave (secondary, shear/transverse, solids only).
Surface waves: Love (horizontal shear, faster surface wave); Rayleigh (rolling, elliptical motion). Surface waves cause most damage.
Magnitude (energy released): Richter (ML, 1935), Moment magnitude (Mw) — preferred. +1 magnitude = 10× amplitude, ≈ 32× energy.
Intensity (effects/damage at a place): Modified Mercalli (MMI), I–XII; MSK scale.
Seismograph records ground motion; accelerograph records acceleration → PGA (peak ground acceleration).
Pakistan tectonics: Indian plate colliding with Eurasian plate (north); Arabian plate subducting under Eurasian at Makran (south-west).

b: Ductility; strong column – weak beam; regular & symmetric plan/elevation.
Avoid: soft storey, short-column effect, torsional irregularity, heavy roofs, re-entrant corners.
Shear walls, bracing, base isolation, dampers (viscous, friction, tuned mass damper).
Detailing: closely spaced stirrups near joints, 135° hooks, confinement, proper lap splices.
Masonry: seismic bands (plinth, lintel, roof/gable), confined masonry, vertical bars at corners.
Liquefaction: loose, saturated sandy soils lose strength in shaking. Remedies: compaction, drainage, stone columns, grouting, deep (pile) foundations.
Tsunami: caused by vertical seafloor displacement (subduction earthquakes), submarine landslides, volcanoes; speed ≈ 700–800 km/h in deep ocean.
Types: riverine (fluvial), flash flood, urban (pluvial), coastal / storm surge, GLOF, dam-break.
Return period: T = 1/P. Probability of at least one exceedance in n years: R = 1 − (1 − 1/T)ⁿ.
Rational formula: Q = CIA/360 (Q in m³/s, I in mm/h, A in hectares) — small catchments.
Spillways designed for PMF (Probable Maximum Flood) for large dams.
Structural measures: dams & reservoirs, levees/embankments (bunds), flood walls, spurs/groynes, channel improvement, diversion channels, retention basins, check dams.
Non-structural measures: floodplain zoning, flood forecasting & warning, flood insurance, flood-proofing, watershed management/afforestation, relocation.

💡 Exam point: GLOF = glacial lake outburst flood — a major threat in Gilgit-Baltistan & Chitral (thousands of glacial lakes).
Mitigation: rainwater harvesting, small dams, efficient irrigation (drip/sprinkler), drought-resistant crops, karez systems.
Names by region: Cyclone (Indian Ocean), Hurricane (Atlantic, NE Pacific), Typhoon (NW Pacific).
Rotation: anticlockwise in Northern Hemisphere, clockwise in Southern. Calm centre = eye.

Mitigation: retaining walls, gabions, surface & sub-surface drainage, rock bolts, soil nailing, benching/terracing, reducing slope angle, vegetation.

Definition (Brundtland Report, "Our Common Future", 1987, WCED): development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
Three pillars: Environmental, Social, Economic. Some add a 4th: Cultural / Institutional.
Triple Bottom Line (TBL): People, Planet, Profit (John Elkington, 1994).
Inter-generational equity: fairness between present and future generations. Intra-generational equity: fairness within the present generation.
Weak sustainability: natural capital can be replaced by man-made capital. Strong sustainability: critical natural capital cannot be substituted.
Carrying capacity: maximum population an environment can support indefinitely.
Ecological footprint: land/water area needed to supply resources and absorb waste; unit = global hectare (gha). Earth Overshoot Day: date humanity uses up the year's renewable resources.
Precautionary principle (Rio Principle 15): lack of full scientific certainty is no reason to delay preventive action.
Polluter Pays principle (Rio Principle 16): polluter bears the cost of pollution.
Decoupling: economic growth without matching rise in resource use / emissions.
Circular economy: make–use–return (vs linear take–make–dispose). Cradle-to-cradle (closed loop) vs cradle-to-grave.
3R: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle (extended: Refuse, Repair, Refurbish, Recover).
Waste hierarchy (most to least preferred): Prevention → Reuse → Recycling → Recovery (energy) → Disposal (landfill).
Planetary boundaries: 9 boundaries (Rockström et al., 2009, Stockholm Resilience Centre); 7 of 9 reported crossed in the 2025 Planetary Health Check.

HDI (UNDP): life expectancy, education (mean & expected years of schooling), GNI per capita (PPP). Range 0–1.
MPI (Multidimensional Poverty Index): UNDP + OPHI; health, education, living standards.
Gini coefficient: income inequality (0 = perfect equality, 1 = max inequality); from Lorenz curve.
Green GDP: GDP adjusted for environmental degradation/resource depletion.
Carbon footprint: total GHG emissions in t CO₂e. 1 carbon credit = 1 tonne CO₂e.
Carbon neutral: emissions balanced by offsets. Net zero: all GHGs reduced to minimum and residual removed.
Cement industry ≈ 7–8 % of global CO₂; most from clinker (calcination of CaCO₃ + fuel).
SCMs reduce clinker: fly ash, GGBS (slag), silica fume, metakaolin, rice husk ash.
Low-carbon options: blended cements, LC3 (limestone calcined clay cement), geopolymer concrete (no OPC; fly ash/slag + alkali activator), recycled aggregate concrete (RAC).
Embodied energy/carbon: energy/emissions to extract, make, transport, build. Operational energy: energy during building use (usually larger over life).
Low embodied energy: timber, stone, earth (adobe, rammed earth, CSEB). High: aluminium, steel, glass, cement.
4 stages: Goal & Scope → Inventory Analysis (LCI) → Impact Assessment (LCIA) → Interpretation.

Energy: passive solar design, correct orientation, insulation, shading, daylighting, natural ventilation, solar PV, Net Zero Energy Building (NZEB).
Water: rainwater harvesting, greywater recycling, low-flow fixtures, groundwater recharge.
Urban drainage: SUDS / LID — permeable pavements, green roofs, swales, bioretention, detention ponds.
Urban heat island mitigation: cool/green roofs, tree cover, reflective pavements.
Transport: Transit-Oriented Development (TOD), BRT, mass transit, non-motorised transport (walking, cycling).
C&D waste: segregation, recycling of rubble as aggregate, design for deconstruction.

Green Building Code of Pakistan 2023: Released by PEC (24 May 2023), based on the 2021 International Green Construction Code; complements Building Code of Pakistan 2021 (IBC-based).
Sustainable materials: Fly-ash/slag cements (less clinker), recycled aggregate, AAC blocks, compressed earth blocks, bamboo, low-VOC paints, solar-reflective roofing.
Rating systems: LEED (USA), BREEAM (UK), EDGE (IFC — used in Pakistan for green housing/finance).
💡 Exam point: Cement production emits ≈ 0.8–0.9 t CO₂ per tonne of clinker — reducing clinker factor is a key sustainability lever.
Pakistan: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act (PEPA) 1997, Section 12 — IEE/EIA mandatory before construction.
IEE (Initial Environmental Examination): smaller projects, less significant impacts. EIA: major projects with significant impacts.
After 18th Amendment (2010): environment devolved → provincial EPAs and provincial acts (e.g. Punjab, Sindh, KP, Balochistan).
IEE/EIA Review Regulations 2000: Schedule I (IEE), Schedule II (EIA).
EIA steps: Screening → Scoping → Baseline study → Impact prediction → Mitigation & EMP → Public consultation/hearing → Review → Decision (NOC) → Monitoring & audit.
EMP = Environmental Management Plan. SEA (Strategic Environmental Assessment) = for policies, plans, programmes.
NEQS: National Environmental Quality Standards (effluents, emissions, ambient air, drinking water, noise).

Programmes: Ten Billion Tree Tsunami, Clean Green Pakistan, Recharge Pakistan, Living Indus (2022), Protected Areas Initiative.
Alternative & Renewable Energy (ARE) Policy 2019: 20 % RE by 2025, 30 % by 2030 (excluding large hydro).
Key climate threats: floods, glacier melt & GLOFs, heatwaves, drought, sea-level rise (Indus delta), smog, water scarcity.
